title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
content: ReAct prompt engineering enables language models to generate reasoning traces and task-specific actions simultaneously. Interleaving thoughts with external tool calls significantly reduces hallucination and preserves goal focus across multi-step execution chains.
author: Yao et al.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
content: Reflexion equips agents with episodic memory buffers where linguistic self-reflections are stored after failures. Rather than fine-tuning weights, agents learn from feedback trials, reducing repeated tool invocation errors by 44%.
author: Shinn et al.

title: Enterprise Multi-Agent Economics and Latency Report
content: Multi-agent collaborative swarms introduce 2.4x to 3.8x token multiplication compared to direct prompt chains. While task accuracy increases for branching research tasks, operational cost multiplies rapidly if uncontrolled gossip protocol routing is used.
author: Stanford HAI & Enterprise AI Alliance

title: Human-in-the-Loop Interception Patterns for Destructive Tool Execution
content: Autonomous agents interacting with production datastores and external broadcast endpoints require asynchronous human authorization. Human approval gates eliminate 98% of destructive action regressions with a median queue delay of 4.2 minutes.
author: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)

title: Empirical Study of LLM Hallucination Rates in Automated Information Retrieval
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) coupled with strict schema validation drops factual citation hallucinations from 18.2% down to 2.1%. Cross-referencing multiple verified public sources prevents single-corpus bias.
author: ACM Computing Surveys
